summary: PROPOSED Civics tree for Director review. Keeps all seven existing civics unchanged (keys 1001-1007; capability blocks re-stated, census's auto-filled owner corrected) and adds 42 micro-civics (practices, institutions, policies in eight strands) and 18 macro-civics (regime forms defined as sets of micro modules: content only in M6 per D-V, adopted in M8 per D-D). No new civic enters any ratified gate (research stage, Age CORE, tax edict, university); macros are leaves (nothing requires them, none requires another) and never Age facts. Every promise names an owner and milestone; regime:/policy: grants and new entities are IMPLEMENTATION DEFERRED because the loader lets a civic unlock only institutions. The research-stage civic atom (legal_code_roman) is kept with a measured CP pacing guarantee; decoupling it from the knowledge stage is the pre-registered remedy. A structural finding: coined_wage is de facto required for A5 entry until M7 (gate audit G-06). All historical anchors are INFERENCE (web retrieval unavailable this session).

meta.costUnit: CP if D-061 is ratified, otherwise RP
meta.costUnitNote: Costs are stated in points with U = 92.4 (BaseCost = U × 2^magnitude). If D-061 is ratified with a civics constant U_c ≠ U (m6-spec §3.2 PROPOSED), every civic cost scales by U_c/U and no magnitude changes.
designRules: R-C1 Distinct tree: no civic copies a technology node; a civic may require technology where the knowledge is causally needed (exposure edge civic→technology); no technology prerequisite names a civic (V04 fence untouched).
R-C2 No new civic enters the prerequisite closure of a ratified gate — the research stage, every Age CORE fact, the tax edict, inst.university (checked: 0).
R-C3 Macro civics are leaves: nothing requires a macro and no macro requires a macro (no regime ladder); 10 of 18 carry OR routes in their own prerequisites.
R-C4 No civic is added to any Age fact; macros are never Age facts; no Age entry grants a civic (I-6, V-08).

R-C5 I-7 tagging: progressionRole is gate · age-supporting · module · optional · regime-form; an 'optional' civic is in no gate closure and no macro closure, so no macro's prerequisites are reachable only through optional nodes (checked).

R-C6 Non-orphan under the current loader: every new civic carries a capability string (ResearchContent.cs:591-600); institution unlocks are listed only where an existing entity's requirement names the civic (reverse index, :1246-1255) — so none until a re-point is ruled.

R-C7 Every promise names an owner system and a milestone; promises needing a representation the loader lacks (regime:/policy: grants, new inst.* entities) are IMPLEMENTATION DEFERRED (Civics may unlock only Institution entities, ResearchContent.cs:1240-1242).

R-C8 Effects change conditions, never outcomes (ADR-019 addendum; law 2): each deferred effect names the equation, predicate or verb it will enter; no bonuses, no policy cards (V-29); governments are module sets, not enums or bonus bundles (Spine :85; D-042 §5).
R-C9 No civic depends on a treasury (V-22; CR-008): central_banking is knowledge-only; social insurance and public debt are rejected candidates.

R-C10 Costs: six factors in quarter steps; the Age enters only as the modal prior inside difficulty and institutional (digest C-04, C-14); prereq_complexity by top-level conjuncts with an OR group counted once (C-10); a costAnalog and a per-factor note; no cost chosen to hit pacing (C-23).

R-C11 Ids are snake_case and unique against every node id and every entity short id (a node id equal to an institution short id is resolved as the node, ResearchContent.cs:1147-1153); display names are unique.
R-C12 Every new emerged text carries an era marker and no must-hold prerequisite is dated later (heuristic of ResearchContentTests.cs:486-525) — checked; the 83 marker-free pin is unaffected.

R-C13 Civics carry no branch (ResearchContent.cs:422-445); strands are a civic-block field, not subtrees (D-044 R3). The UI makes one Civics lane per distinct domain (ResearchTreeLayout.cs:125-131): all new civics keep domain 'governance' (existing vocabulary) — strand lanes are an OPEN DECISION (OD-10).

agePrior._doc: modal difficulty / institutional per Age, FACT@edba2b5 (digest C-14)

costRubric.micro: novelty 1.0 (0.5 only for an extension of an existing civic: tax_farming, laws_of_war); difficulty = Age prior (±0.25 with a note); material 0; institutional = Age prior ±0.25–0.5 with a note (civics are institutional by nature: the seven existing civics sit 0–0.5 above the prior); breadth 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 by downstream scope; prereq_complexity by convention.
costRubric.macro: novelty 1.0; difficulty = Age prior; material 0; institutional = Age prior + 0.25…0.75 (coordination of several modules, noted per form); breadth 1.0 (1.5 where the form reorganizes every civil domain: feudal_monarchy, military_rule); prereq_complexity by convention.
costRubric.referenceMicro: 1.0 + difficulty prior + institutional prior + 0.5 + 0.5 — the magnitude of a typical two-requirement, one-domain micro at the modal priors (A1 2.0 · A2 2.75 · A3 3.75 · A4 4.25 · A5 4.75 · A6 5.0 · A7 5.5 · A8 6.5 · A9 7.5).
costRubric.existingAnchors: taxation 3.5 (1,050) · law_code 3.75 (1,240) · coined_wage 3.75 (1,240) · legal_code_roman 4.75 (2,490) · joint_stock 5.0 (2,960) · patent 5.5 (4,180) · census 5.75 (4,970)

costBalance.rule: macro ≈ the same Age's micro + 0.5…1.0 magnitude, i.e. ×1.4…×2 in cost
justification: Breadth: a form reorganizes several domains at once (participation, administration, legitimacy), so its downstream scope is civilization-wide where a micro's is one or two domains — the +0.5 breadth step.
Institutional coordination: a form binds several modules into one arrangement — +0.25…0.75 over the institutional prior, noted per form.
Difficulty stays at the Age prior: the hard part of a form (its modules) is already paid in the modules' own costs; the form's closure cost = modules + premium (meta.macroClosures).

Bounded at +1.0: forms are optional alternatives; a larger premium would make 'optional' mean 'unreachable' for a civilization that develops several modules, and a premium below +0.5 would make a form a free relabelling of its modules.
costBalance.measuredResult: Premium of the macro median over the micro median: A2 +0.5 · A3 +0.875 · A4 +0.75 · A5 +0.5 · A6 +0.625 · A7 +0.75 · A8 +0.5 · A9 +0.375 (A9 has a single micro, central_planning, itself economy-wide; against the A9 reference micro the premium is +0.875). See table.

cpPacingTolerances.status: PROPOSED tolerances for T6.3 acceptance (D-061.3 and D-061.8 are ruled together, docket C.1)
cpPacingTolerances.nature: An A/B attribution comparison between the CP world and the one-pool twin (TestConfigs.PreCivicsPoints) on the same seeds — not a calibration corridor: no coefficient is tuned to hit it and its only consequence is a structural remedy (m6-spec §3.3; digest C-29).
cpPacingTolerances.protocol: Seeds 1, 2, 42, 7; horizon 1,630 turns; drivers (i) the AI polity (sim run --founded --ai-empires 1) and (ii) the --auto cheapest research driver. Measure T_tech (stage technology atoms complete), T_lcr (legal_code_roman complete), T_stage, T_A5core, T_A5entry, T_A7entry; civic lag L = T_stage − T_tech.

tolerances.rule: every polity that reaches the research stage (and A5 entry) in the twin also reaches it in the CP world within the horizon
T_stage(CP) ≤ T_stage(twin) + 10 turns on every seed and driver (≈1.4 % of the measured 702-716)
median L = 0 and max L ≤ 5 turns over seeds × drivers (today L = 0 with 66-67 turns of slack)
T_A5entry(CP) ≤ T_A5entry(twin) + 10 turns — covers the CORE civic legal_code_roman and the structural a5_wages civic coined_wage

Before any run, the candidate D-061.3 CP equation (its own inputs; never a fraction or split of RP — cp-economy-proposal.md §2) must, in the static model (tools/cp_gate.py -> data/balance-cp-gate.json), accumulate the gate civics' closure (law_code + legal_code_roman = 3,730 CP) plus a 10,000-CP detour between the first writing completion and the one-pool stage turn on every seed and driver, i.e. pass P2 with detourCP = 10,000. ESTIMATE (static model). Replaces the earlier 'CP_turn >= 0.30 x RP_turn' form, which stated CP as a ratio of RP.
if P1-P4 fail: (1) the AI civics lane works gate civics first; (2) revise D-061.3 CP inputs; (3) Option B. Never a civic or technology cost change (C-23).

T_taxation(CP) <= max(T_taxation(twin) + 10, T_A3entry(twin)) on every seed and driver, so the operational tax edict (knowledge AND Age III AND seat) opens no later than in the twin. MEASURED twin: taxation 328-339, A3 entry 412-425 (AI). ESTIMATE under the placeholder CP equation: 329-351 (cp_gate.py, scale 1).

cpPacingTolerances.humanPlayers: The tolerances bind AI and scripted drivers. A human who neglects civics delays the stage by choice; the stage lock must name the civic prerequisite across trees (legal_code_roman playerCommunication).

civVILessons: Two currencies, two trees, two targets (adopted shape, D-061) — but no flat yields and no policy cards (rejected, V-29).
Give the civics currency something to buy from the first turns: four A1-A2 micro civics and two A2 forms.
Avoid a strict government ladder: forms here are leaves over modules, reachable by OR routes, never prerequisites of each other.
Cross-tree coupling there is through boosts only; here it is one explicit gate (the research stage) plus civic→technology prerequisites — kept explicit and measured.
Government as mechanism: a form is the label of a module set whose effects enter named equations (arch-FGH), not a bundle of bonuses.

workloadByAge._doc: Points by metadata Age (U = 92.4). Matters only if D-061 is NOT ratified: then these costs compete with technology for the one RP pool and the AI's 'cheapest available anywhere' fallback.

closures._doc: Cheapest-closure cost (greedy over OR, an upper bound) of each new civic over the current technology graph plus this proposal; civicClosureCost is the part payable in CP under D-061.

technologyDependencies._doc: Technology nodes named in new civic prerequisites (civic→technology exposure edges, allowed; no technology names a civic). integrate.py rewrites atoms of merged/replaced nodes; a split must keep the key on the part these civics need, or tell D12.

macroClosures._doc: directModules = the civic atoms of the form's own prerequisite; civicsOnAnyRoute = every civic ancestor over all OR routes; closureCost / civicClosureCost = the cheapest route (greedy over OR, an upper bound) and its CP-payable part; ownCost = the form's own premium node.

civic.concept: A one-party state led by a communist party that claims to rule on behalf of the working class under Marxist–Leninist doctrine, with state or collective ownership of the means of production and central economic planning.
civic.states: Researched/Available: the form becomes eligible — its module civics are its prerequisites; Adopted: the polity adopts the form's module set by an M8 act (none in M6, D-D); Active: the module set latched in force; the government label is derived from it and never read by a mechanism (arch-FGH §2.1-2.2); Realized: the derived label shown in the chronicle and the INSTITUTIONS lens.
civic.eligibility: Completion makes the marxist–leninist state form eligible for adoption in M8 (its modules: mass_political_party AND central_planning).
civic.currentEffect: None today — PROPOSED node, not in content. Once added: the completion row only (I-1); its capability string appears as knowledge. No adoption, no active effect (D-D).
civic.deferredEffect: M8 adoption of the module set mass_political_party AND central_planning; the government label is derived, never stored or read by a mechanism (arch-FGH §2.1-2.2).
civic.ageRelation: A9 metadata (Modern / Contemporary); never an Age fact (CORE or supporting); no Age entry grants it (I-6, V-08)
civic.aiValuation: M6: fallback only (no adoption exists, so a form has no M6 value to an AI). M8: valued by the AI's regime evaluation from the polity's own state (its realized modules, classes and reach) — never from another polity's civics state (metamorphic fence, I-9).

crossLaneRequests.request: Keep bill_of_exchange, paper_money, coinage_electrum, trade and stamp_seal in Technology (relocation analysed and declined).
crossLaneRequests.reason: Each is knowledge of an instrument or technique; moving a node between trees re-keys it and old saves lose it (no alias/remap, engine audit Q14). Their institutional halves are civics: commercial_law, central_banking, appointed_officials/taxation.

crossLaneRequests.request: If cuneiform/hieroglyphic/chinese_script, paper, printing_press, paper_money, telegraph or trade are split, keep the key on the part carrying full writing, paper, the press/public sphere, printed notes, electric signalling and formal exchange — or tell D12.
crossLaneRequests.reason: They are prerequisites of 9 new civics (meta.technologyDependencies); integrate.py rewrites only merged/replaced atoms.

crossLaneRequests.request: Keep double_entry in Technology; its subtree placement (natural_science) is D04's call.
crossLaneRequests.reason: An accounting technique, not an institution; it names a6_finance (supporting) and has no civic half.

crossLaneRequests.request: Keep standard_weights, surveying and calendar_lunar in Technology; phrase surveying's 'land register' capability as knowledge (measuring and recording boundaries) without tax effects.
crossLaneRequests.reason: The public register of title and dues is the civic land_registry; calendar_lunar, surveying and hindu_arabic are prerequisites of organized_priesthood, land_registry and official_statistics.

crossLaneRequests.request: If cereal_cultivation or sheep_goat is split, keep the keys on the domestication parts.
crossLaneRequests.reason: hereditary_rank and organized_priesthood require a storable food surplus through them.

crossLaneRequests.request: cartography is a prerequisite of general_staff; infra.courier_relay already covers the state courier system's physical half (D12 rejected a duplicate 'royal post' civic).
crossLaneRequests.reason: Avoid a duplicate courier node in either tree.

crossLaneRequests.request: Do not add technology nodes for standing armies, conscription, general staffs or land-for-service; if unit families need a professional-army precondition, express it through the M7 recruitment contract reading the civic's completion, not a technology prerequisite naming a civic.
crossLaneRequests.reason: They are civics (institutions); a technology prerequisite naming a civic breaks the V04 fence.
